description: Shared ZeroAlloc Renovate defaults. Extend from a repo with:
"extends": ["config:recommended", "github>ZeroAlloc-Net/.github"]
and drop that repo's own "schedule" — this replaces it.
Updates flow continuously, but nothing is raised until a release has been out
for three days. That is the point at which a bad or yanked release has usually
been found, so it buys the same protection a weekly batch window did without
the batching: an update published on Tuesday arrives Friday rather than
waiting for the following Monday.
Security fixes opt out of both the wait and any schedule. minimumReleaseAge is
set back to null under vulnerabilityAlerts, because otherwise the three-day
wait would inherit and delay exactly the updates that must not wait.
schedule: [] means 'any time', so a security PR is still raised immediately
even in a repo that keeps a schedule of its own. Without it, a repo scheduled
'before 6am on monday' parks security fixes under Awaiting Schedule until the
next window — which is how ZeroAlloc.Serialisation sat with a high-severity
MessagePack advisory while audit-as-error made main unbuildable, unnoticed
because CI only runs on push and pull_request.
semanticCommitType fix, rather than Renovate's default chore: release-please
treats chore as non-releasable, so a security fix would merge to main and
never ship — the package consumers restore would stay vulnerable. fix cuts a
patch release.
internalChecksFilter is left at its default of strict, so updates still inside
the three-day wait are held back rather than raised and then blocked.
vulnerabilityAlerts carries no prPriority: Renovate only accepts prPriority
inside packageRules, and renovate-config-validator rejects it here. It was
silently ignored rather than prioritising anything. Security PRs already skip
the three-day wait and any schedule, which is what actually gets them out
quickly; prPriority would only have reordered a queue held back by prConcurrentLimit.
packageRules group each ZeroAlloc family into one PR. Every repo releases with
a single-component release-please manifest, so all the packages it publishes
share one version and ship together — and several of them cannot be upgraded
apart. A source generator bumped without its runtime emits code the older
runtime cannot satisfy: ZeroAlloc.Saga#92 took ZeroAlloc.Mediator.Generator to
v5 on its own and failed with CS0051, while the sibling PR carrying only
ZeroAlloc.Mediator went green. Neither half could merge alone, and no amount
of retrying either PR would have fixed it.
separateMajorMinor is off for these groups. Grouping alone is not enough: a
family whose runtime offers a minor and whose generator offers a major would
still be split back into two PRs by the default major/minor separation, which
is the exact failure this is meant to prevent.
Groups are keyed on the publishing repo rather than the package prefix, which
is why ZeroAlloc.TypeConversions sits in the ORM group — it ships from
ZeroAlloc.ORM at ORM's version, so it moves when ORM moves.
A new ZeroAlloc repo with no rule here keeps today's behaviour of one PR per
package. That is safe for a family with no generator; add a rule when the
repo starts publishing one.
